mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of low FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05), this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects expanding economic activity and consumer confidence, which should positively impact the S&P 500 over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase but the S&P 500 does not show positive returns, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market weakness, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment may decline over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate rises but the S&P 500 shows positive returns, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates stronger economic output, which should lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but the S&P 500 does not show positive returns, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: When both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increase, it signals a strong labor market, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE and PAYEMS increase but the S&P 500 does not show positive returns, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) increase borrowing costs and reduce liquidity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate is high but the S&P 500 shows positive returns, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which should lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If retail sales increase but the S&P 500 does not show positive returns, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows but inflation (CPIAUCSL) also rises, the net effect on corporate earnings and consumer spending can be negative, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 grows and CPIAUCSL rises but the S&P 500 does not show negative returns, this hypothesis is rejected.
